title: What If an Interstellar Comet Flew Past Us? 3I/ATLAS Did

scenes.text: What if a visitor from another star flew past Earth? In 2025, one did.
It was comet 3I/ATLAS, only the third object ever seen that came from outside our solar system.
It moved at roughly 60 kilometers a second, fast enough to cross the Atlantic in about 90 seconds.
Its nucleus is somewhere between 440 meters and 5.6 kilometers wide, according to Hubble.
At its closest on December 19, 2025, it was 270 million kilometers away, nearly twice the Sun's distance.
It posed no threat, and it is already heading back out of the solar system forever.
